v1.20.0 closes the 1.19 series. Its thread is that every number in the books can be followed to
where it came from, and trusted when it gets there: a posted row is never deleted, a report's frozen
figures carry the ledger lines behind them, a statement figure opens on the accounts it was summed
from, and a sweep of the ledger fixed every way a figure was found to go wrong. Around that, the
ledger gained what a finance lead runs a company on — receivables and payables by due date,
management dimensions, an account register — and the group gained a life of its own: a member can be
bought partway through the year, the parent can buy more of it, and the consolidated statements are
a report like any company's.

Covers everything since v1.19.0; the 1.19.x patches carried generated changelogs.

## Every figure traces to its lines

**Posted rows are permanent.** A correction that rebuilds what was posted in an open month — a
reconciling item's restate, a replaced opening balance, the consolidation engine's opening — used to
delete the posted entries and write new ones, so nothing that referenced the old rows could resolve
them again. They are now superseded: kept with their ids, marked, and linked to the rows that
replaced them.

**A report's columns freeze as the calendar closes.** A saved report's column for a closed period
keeps the facts written at its close and is never rewritten; a column for an open period refreshes
as postings land. Every fact carries its own provenance: a pivoted figure names the accounts that
foot to it, a roll-up the concepts and weights it summed, a derived value its computation, and a
frozen pivot hashes the lines it was made from.

**The holon with lineage.** A report downloads as a holon whose fourth graph, `#lineage`, is the
ledger behind its frozen figures: each figure derived from its accounts, each account's contribution
made of the lines it summed, each line reaching its entry, transaction, event and counterparty. It is
built on download for the graph's own members and never crosses the graph boundary as rows; a
figure whose reconstruction misses its frozen hash is named as omitted rather than served wrong.

**From a figure to its accounts, and an account to its lines.** `live-financial-statement` takes
`include_sources`, and every row says how it was made and which accounts, in which entity, it was
summed from. The GraphQL `accountRegister` reads one account's posted lines in order, each with the
balance it leaves and the entry and event behind it. An event lists the entries it posted, and an
entry names its event.

## The ledger sweep

A pass over the ledger's write and read paths, each defect pinned by a real-database test that
fails on the old code:

- **Events and the close.** A committed event always writes its ledger rows; template amounts round
  to whole cents in integers, so no amount is too long to divide; a template's preview and a
  reversal's preview agree with the write.
- **Statements and reads.** A sale or purchase with cash down counts its cash once on the cash flow;
  a disposal retires the schedule's months after it and leaves the period's charge alone; statement
  reads stay in their year and their entity.
- **Groups and feeds.** A subsidiary's bank feed opens its own entity's books; a calendar's start
  cannot move under a first close; ledger writes act on the entity whose books they touch;
  counterparty defaults are kept per entity.
- **A bank line that arrives after its month closed is held, not dropped.** It is written held, and
  the entity's next close waits on `held_bank_lines` until someone reopens the month or closes over
  it.
- **Smaller loose ends:** a closed month's flow re-tag re-stamps its statements; a stale outstanding
  line on a statement reconciliation is shown as not counted; every tenant carries the event-row
  foreign keys.

## Receivables, payables and dimensions

**Due dates, open items and aging.** Invoices and bills carry their due date, from QuickBooks or the
event. Open receivables and payables read as of any date, aged into buckets, with a tie-out of the
open items to the control account. A payment settles invoices and bills document by document, from
QuickBooks' linked transactions or the inbox's settlement picker.

**Management dimensions.** Department, class, location, project or an axis of a company's own tag
journal lines, one member per axis. Events, bank lines and schedules carry them onto the lines they
write; QuickBooks classes and locations are captured on sync. The income statement reads by member
or with a column per member, and the trial balance by one member.

## The group

**A consolidated report is the consolidation entity's.** A report made for the consolidation entity
is the group's consolidated statements, named for the group and listed on the parent. Group reads
count each member for its own months, and the group close keeps its first-month opening, reversals
and leavers straight.

**A member bought from its owners.** `record-acquisition` takes what the parent paid a member's
sellers, with the basis and any fair values, and drafts the acquisition in the consolidation entity:
the excess over the parent's share of the member's equity at acquisition to step-ups and goodwill,
the outside owners' share of what they add as noncontrolling interest. The engine reads the
consideration as the parent's investment, so the elimination proceeds; until it is recorded, the
residual says it is pre-acquisition. In the month the member joins, its cash is the group's cash
acquired, an investing inflow, and the group's cash flow opens where its previous month closed.

**The parent buys more.** `record-ownership-change` records a higher share from a month and the price
paid to the outside owners, staying on full consolidation. ASC 810 makes it an equity transaction:
the price above the book value bought goes against the investment, the share bought of the member's
results moves out of noncontrolling interest, and the difference is the parent's equity, with no
gain or loss. The engine reads each member's share as of the month, so earlier months keep theirs.

**The outside owners' share, read.** The GraphQL `allocationShare` and `allocationOverrides` read a
member's month as the engine does — its result, the pro-rata share, the override and the share the
entries use.

## Statements

**The cash flow opens and closes on cash.** Every indirect cash flow now starts from beginning cash
and ends at ending cash, the ASU 2016-18 total of cash and restricted cash, with the check that
beginning plus net change equals ending a finding on the statement. The export presents it as the
equity roll-forward is presented.

**A filed report downloads as filed.** A report's bundle is built from its own fact sets, on the
structures they pinned, whatever Reporting Style the company has moved to since. The `rollforward`
information-block arm, whose filter engine never ran, is removed.

## Schedules

The schedule engine's foundations were fixed — terminate and rebuild, the plug month, the originating
event, the credit account — and schedules now round-trip: a schedule's definition comes back on its
envelope and saves through `rebuild-schedule`, `preview-schedule` shows the roll-forward before
anything is written, a schedule that would move the wrong way is refused, and recreating one with
posted entries says which months. Loan amortization runs as a schedule: an effective-interest table
with the day-count conventions the books use, accrued monthly or split from the payment.

## AI clients and sharing

**An AI proposes a posting rule; a person approves it.** An event handler created through an AI
client is a suggestion that takes no part in matching until a person approves it, and an AI client's
change to what an approved handler matches or books makes it a suggestion again. The GraphQL
`eventHandlers` read lists them with `awaitingApproval`.

**Where a report went.** The GraphQL `reportShares` read shows the sender every delivery of a report
and its revocation; revoking holds a lock, and a report shared in reads the copy it received.

## Platform

- Subscription lifecycle handling and the write-path checks on graphs were hardened.
- The published graph limits are the ones the platform enforces.
- Materialization holds off while a tier upgrade moves a graph's volume.
- CI runs its static gates beside the suite; logs no longer report a cache flush as an
  authorization denial.

## Migrations

Extensions `0056` (superseded rows), `0057` (event due dates), `0058` (event discharges), `0059`
(fact columns frozen by the calendar), `0060` (event-row foreign keys), `0061` (the cash total on the
cash flow: a library data migration that refreshes `public` and resyncs every tenant), `0062` (the
`ownership_change` adjustment kind); platform `2e9def42942a` (drops unenforced graph limit columns).

## Clients

The `robosystems-client` minors through this series track these additions in both SDKs: the account
register, dimensions, aging, allocation shares, `recordAcquisition`, `recordOwnershipChange`,
`listEventHandlers`, `listReportShares` and `listElements({ includeInactive })`, with the
`preview-schedule` operation and the new schedule fields in the generated tier.
